text:
**Architecture Overview**

sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 with three processes.

The reader process connects to Postgres. It streams rows in batches. Each batch holds a fixed number of rows. The reader sends each batch to the converter.

The converter turns each batch into a Parquet row group. A row group holds the column data in the Parquet format. The converter collects row groups into one Parquet file. Then it sends the file to the uploader.

The uploader writes the file to S3 as a multipart object. A multipart object is one object that S3 builds from many parts. The uploader sends each part in a separate request. If a request fails, the uploader retries the part.

The three processes run at the same time. This design keeps the data in motion and limits the memory use.
